nodes.name: Instantly: room left?
nodes.notes: Runs FIRST on purpose. Sourcing is free and enrichment is not, so the cheap check that can fail the whole run goes before anything metered. Skipping this is how you pay LinkFinder for leads Instantly will refuse.

parameters.jsCode:
const cfg = $input.first().json;
return cfg.categories.map(slug => ({ json: { ...cfg, slug } }));

nodes.name: G2: products in category
nodes.notes: The official API, not a scraper. G2 sits behind Cloudflare and scraping it breaks their terms; this token is already yours and does not get blocked. Its one real limit is that a buyer-scoped account sees only a category's top products -- which is exactly why the category list must stay narrow.

nodes.name: One prospect at a time
nodes.notes: Batch size 1. The LinkFinder lookup fails about half the time with a status message rather than an error, so each prospect needs its own retry path.

nodes.name: LinkFinder: decision maker
nodes.notes: n8n's own retry does NOT catch this endpoint's real failure: it answers HTTP 200 with a fake person whose name is a status message, so nothing here looks like an error. The next node is what actually detects it.

nodes.name: Real person, empty, or provider down?

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ campaign: $json.campaignId, email: $json.email, first_name: $json.firstName, last_name: $json.lastName, company_name: $json.company, website: $json.domain, skip_if_in_workspace: true, custom_variables: { category: $json.category, reviewCount: String($json.reviewCount), title: $json.title } }) }}

nodes.name: Instantly: add lead
nodes.notes: category and reviewCount MUST travel with the lead. The opener reads 'I was going through the {{category}} category on G2 and {{companyName}} came up with {{reviewCount}} reviews' -- a lead missing either renders a broken first line to a real person.
